about: The Atlas of Forms: how uniformly Meta's Muse Image (and Stable Diffusion XL) draws 135 everyday things, against people's drawings from Google Quick, Draw!, measured with Meta DINOv2. Derived statistics only: no drawings and no embeddings. ratio = model spread / people's spread (below 1 = more uniform than people); rank 1 = most Platonic. Muse's numbers are its defaults for one doodle prompt; asked for variety, Muse can draw more varied pictures (docs/plato.md).
attribution: Human drawings: Google Quick, Draw! dataset (Google Creative Lab), CC BY 4.0, https://github.com/googlecreativelab/quickdraw-dataset
prompt: A quick simple doodle sketch of {phrase}, black marker on plain white, like a 20-second drawing, no text, no shading.
spread: mean pairwise cosine distance between DINOv2 CLS embeddings of ink-cropped pictures
human_reference: the first 200 drawings with recognized=true in each Quick, Draw! simplified file, rendered at 256 px; human_spread is the mean over 200 random subsets of the model's n; human_spread_all is the spread of all 200 (independent of n)

predictors.note: EXPLORATORY (pre-registered as such): bootstrap 95% CIs over concepts (5,000) and permutation p; no correction for multiple tests.
predictors.P1_note: The ratio's denominator is people's spread, so its correlation with people's spread is partly mechanical; the Muse-spread correlation is the informative one.
